study_identification.title: Multivariate brain-cognition associations in euthymic bipolar disorder

study_characteristics.study_objective: To examine multivariate associations between cortical thickness and core cognitive functions (processing speed, attention, and executive function) in euthymic bipolar disorder, using a normative modeling approach to estimate brain abnormalities.

dataset_name.answer: A multi-site aggregated dataset from public sources (HCP, OpenBHB, OASIS-3, Cam-CAN) and a local cohort (NCL).

hc_age.answer: Normative model: mean 32.64, sd 19.39, range 5-95. Matched controls: mean 48.46, sd 11.80

hc_sex.answer: Normative model: 50.3% female (3194 F). Matched controls: 12 F (46%)

imaging_modality.answer: T1-weighted MRI; T2-FLAIR (for pial surface refinement)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer v6.0 (recon-all); dcm2niix; R (mgcv package for harmonization)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Visual quality inspections on a sub-sample, manual corrections of pial surface. Outlier removal from normative-HC data (residuals > 5 median absolute deviations, n=393 excluded). One HC excluded due to poor quality T1w image.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Harmonized normative-HC data by regressing age, sex, and scanning protocol (site as a random effect) on cortical thickness using a generalized additive model (GAM) in R (mgcv package). BD data adjusted using the prediction from the normative model, with site correction informed by the site offset estimated for BLISS HCs.

modeling_method.answer: Generalized Additive Model (GAM) for harmonization, then z-scoring based on the normative mean and standard deviation.

response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness (68 ROIs from Desikan-Killiany atlas)

predictor_effects.answer: Age and Sex as fixed effects, Site as a random effect in the GAM for harmonization.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The model explicitly handles site effects using a random effect in a GAM, and models the non-linear effect of age.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS, for each ROI by regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (i.e., site; as a random effect) on cortical thickness using a generalised additive model.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not mention any form of cross-validation or other non-independent validation of the normative model.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Our sample size was too small to split into training and test datasets to perform an additional cross-validation step, which is often advised to validate results of CCA.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper does not mention validating the model on an independent dataset from the same domain.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not mention validating the model on a dataset from a different domain.

clinical_dataset.answer: Bipolar Lithium Imaging and Spectroscopy Study (BLISS)

deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores based on the normative model of cortical thickness.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) to assess multivariate associations between neuropsychological performance and cortical thickness. Principal Components Analysis (PCA) was used for dimensionality reduction on the cortical thickness data before CCA. Permutation testing was used to validate the CCA results.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Impairments in processing speed and executive function were most strongly associated with abnormal cortical thickness in temporal regions (left inferior temporal, right entorhinal, right temporal pole) in euthymic BD, although the primary CCA result was not statistically significant.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Euthymic BD patients (n=56) showed cognitive impairments and cortical thinning compared to controls. A non-significant trend (p=0.093) in the CCA (correlation=0.86) suggested that poorer processing speed (DSST) and executive function (TMT-B minus TMT-A) were associated with cortical thickness abnormalities in the left inferior temporal (rho=0.406), right entorhinal (rho=0.380), and right temporal pole (rho=0.334) areas.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Modest BD sample size for CCA, limiting statistical power and preventing cross-validation. The neuropsychological battery was not comprehensive. Cognitive impairment estimations were based on a small matched control group, not a large normative sample. The correlational nature of CCA prevents causal inference. The main finding was not statistically significant. Potential confounding effects of lithium treatment were not fully explored.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates the utility of combining normative modeling and multivariate methods (CCA) to investigate complex brain-cognition relationships in psychiatric disorders, even with modest sample sizes.

general_notes.general_notes: The study is a secondary analysis of the BLISS dataset. The normative model was constructed from a large aggregation of public datasets (HCP, OpenBHB, OASIS-3, Cam-CAN) plus a local dataset. The authors note that future research should explore other morphological metrics (volume, surface area) and their covariance.
